children: Welspun Living has approved a capital expenditure of up to ₹3,200 crore through its wholly owned subsidiary, Welspun Home Solutions (WHSL), to ramp up manufacturing capacity and strengthen backward integration.

The proposed expansion will add around 29,000 metric tonnes (MT) of annual terry towel manufacturing capacity, alongside new spinning and weaving facilities and a research and development (R&D) centre, the company said in an exchange filing.
The expansion is expected to be completed by December 31, 2028, as per the filing.
The proposed capex will be funded through an investment of up to ₹800 crore by Welspun Living in WHSL and borrowings of up to ₹2,400 crore by the subsidiary from banks and financial institutions.

The ₹800 crore investment will be made through either 8% non-cumulative optionally convertible redeemable preference shares (NCOCRPS) or optionally convertible debentures (OCDs), in one or more tranches. The OCDs will carry an interest rate of the government securities (G-Sec) yield plus a 1% margin, with a tenure of 20 years.
At the consolidated level, Welspun Living currently has an annual terry towel manufacturing capacity of around 96,000 MT, with capacity utilisation at 83% as of September 30, 2026.

The proposed expansion will add approximately 29,000 MT of annual terry towel capacity. In addition, the company plans to increase its weaving capacity by around 15,000 MT per annum and yarn capacity by approximately 31,000 MT per annum, covering coarse count, fine count and open-end yarn.

The company said the investment is aimed at supporting its growth strategy through capacity expansion and backward integration, while capitalising on demand prospects, scale and cost benefits. The proposed expansion is within Welspun Living's existing business operations.

WHSL will raise up to ₹2,400 crore through term loans from banks and financial institutions to fund the proposed capital expenditure. Welspun Living will provide a corporate guarantee for the borrowings.

The company clarified that there will be no immediate impact on its consolidated debt, except to the extent of the corporate guarantee, should WHSL be unable to meet its repayment obligations. The guarantee will constitute a contingent liability for Welspun Living, stated the exchange filing.
The board of WHSL approved the requisite proposals on November 21, while shareholder approval for the issue of NCOCRPS or OCDs and the proposed borrowings is scheduled to be sought on November 27.

title: Welspun Living plans ₹3,200 crore investment in capacity expansion by December 2028
